The PRA ensures that data requested by the Federal Government can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed. This notice informs the public of the agency's intent to request renewal of the clearance for the IMLS Grants to States Five-Year State Plan Guidelines for State Library Administrative Agencies. The current five-year period covers fiscal years (FYs) 2022-2027. The upcoming five-year period will cover FYs 2028-2032, with Five-Year State Plans due to IMLS on June 30, 2027. A copy of the proposed information collection request can be obtained by contacting the individual listed below in the ADDRESSES section of this notice.

Civil Penalties; Notice of Adjusted Maximum Amounts
summary: In 1990, Congress enacted statutory amendments to adjust the maximum civil penalty amounts authorized under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA), the Federal Hazardous Substances Act (FHSA), and the Flammable Fabrics Act (FFA). On August 14, 2008, the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 2008 (CPSIA) increased the maximum civil penalty amounts to $100,000 for each violation and $15,000,000 for any related series of violations. The CPSIA tied the effective date of the new amounts to the earlier of the date on which final regulations are issued, or 1 year after August 14, 2008. The new amounts became effective on August 14, 2009. The CPSIA also revised the starting date, from December 1, 1994 to December 1, 2011, and December 1 of each fifth calendar year thereafter, on which the Commission must prescribe and publish in the Federal Register, the schedule of maximum authorized penalties. On December 1, 2021, the CPSC published increased maximum authorized civil penalty amounts of $120,000 for each violation and $17,150,000 for any related series of violations. As calculated in accordance with the amendments, the new amounts are $140,000 for each violation and $20,350,000 for any related series of violations.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of engine stall events that occurred on ground in icing weather conditions (freezing fog) during engine acceleration to take-off thrust, or during the take-off phase. This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to provide the flightcrew with a prohibition to follow under certain freezing fog conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A330-202, A330-243, A330-243F, A330-302, A330-323, A330-343, A330-841, and A330-941 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by an investigation that revealed a potential discrepant gap between the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) vent intake panel and horizontal tail plane skin. This proposed AD would require modification of the NACA vent intake panel installation on the horizonal tail plane. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model BD-700-1A10 and BD-700-1A11 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an issue with the heads-up display application (HDA) software in avionics software version 5.8 that could result in the HDA being unable to read errors in the graphical engine chip (GE5) local and frame buffer memory during power-up. This proposed AD would require installing avionics software version 5.9 or later approved software version. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request
Reef Fish Fishery of the Gulf of America; Amendment 63
summary: The Gulf Council (Council) has submitted Amendment 63 to the Fishery Management Plan for the Reef Fish Resources of the Gulf (FMP) (Amendment 63) for review, approval, and implementation by NMFS. If approved, Amendment 63 would, for red grouper in the Gulf of America (Gulf), establish a commercial quota pool under a 3-year pilot program within the Grouper-Tilefish Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) program. The purpose of Amendment 63 is to test whether a new method of distributing a portion of the red grouper commercial quota improves access to red grouper commercial allocation within the IFQ program, reduces bycatch and discards of IFQ species, and enhances economic profitability for quota pool participants.
